d: Steroidogenic acute regulatory protein, which carries cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane; this delivery is the rate-limiting step of steroid synthesis, and ACTH and LH speed it up.
The route used by receptors that lack their own kinase: hormone binding recruits Janus kinase (JAK), which phosphorylates STAT proteins that enter the nucleus; GH, prolactin and EPO signal this way.
A short DNA sequence near a target gene where a hormone-receptor complex for a steroid, thyroid hormone or calcitriol binds to switch transcription on or off.
The liver protein that carries testosterone and estradiol. Estrogen and thyroid hormone raise it, while androgens, obesity and insulin resistance lower it, which changes the free hormone fraction.
A pituitary hormone whose job is to drive another endocrine gland, such as TSH, ACTH, LH or FSH; its level is the first number to read when locating a defect in an axis.
Failure of target cells to respond to a hormone because of a receptor or signaling defect, so the hormone level is high while the patient shows signs of deficiency.
